The invasion and takeover of England by Duke William of Normandy, William the Conqueror, from 1066.

Edward the Confessor died in January 1066 without children, and Harold Godwinson was crowned. In September the Norwegian king Harald Hardrada landed in Yorkshire; Harold beat and killed him at Stamford Bridge, then marched south to meet William, who had landed at Pevensey. At the Battle of Hastings on 14 October Harold was killed and the English army broke.

William was crowned on Christmas Day, but it took until about 1071 to put down English revolts. The results:

  • a new ruling class of Norman and French lords, with the English landholders almost wiped out;
  • stone castles and cathedrals across the country;
  • a French-speaking court for three centuries, which brought thousands of French words into English;
  • the Domesday Book survey of 1086.

It drew England away from the Scandinavian world and toward France, which led to long wars over French lands, down to the Hundred Years' War.
sum: The invasion and takeover of England by Duke William of Normandy, William the Conqueror, from 1066.
